paragraphs: On this page, Animal Breeders (45-2021) is taken as the selection and breeding tasks: matching animals by lineage, traits, and offspring goals, possibly performing artificial insemination, semen handling, animal observation, and pedigree and production record-keeping, and also undertaking feeding and cleaning, purchasing, sales, and showing. Livestock must be checked against the statutory catalog, and the livestock permit is not directly applied to dogs and cats. Actual veterinary care checks the authority of licensed veterinarians, assistant veterinarians, or rural veterinarians and institutional conditions per law; a breeding position title grants no veterinary license.

In one sentence: an agricultural production position that selects and breeds animals by lineage, traits, and offspring goals, performs artificial insemination, and maintains pedigree and breeding records, while also undertaking feeding, cleaning, immunization, and animal health observation.

O*NET lists four task groups: daily feeding and housing management; selection breeding, artificial insemination, and semen handling; health observation and individual records; purchasing, sales, and showing. US tasks do not directly grant China operating or veterinary authorization. Full tasks are in the AI evidence card and the original occupational data.

O*NET 45-2021.00 Animal Breeders: select and breed animals according to their lineage, traits, and offspring, possibly needing to master artificial insemination techniques and equipment use, and possibly involving recording estrus, parturition intervals, or pedigrees. Common job titles include Animal Technician, AI Technician, Artificial Inseminator, Breeder, Dog Breeder, and Large Herd Specialist. The 2022 Dictionary's Livestock Breeders (5-03-01-01) and Poultry Breeders (5-03-01-02) serve only as livestock-and-poultry direction references, not equating all directions such as dogs and cats to a single Chinese occupation. The interest code is RCI (Realistic, Conventional, Investigative).

entries: Daily feeding and housing｜Feeding and cleaning｜Feed and water animals, clean and disinfect housing, cages, and grounds, build cages and fences, and adjust housing temperature.
Breeding and mating｜Selection and artificial insemination｜Select breeding animals and semen samples by lineage, traits, and offspring goals, and inseminate females with the semen to carry out mating.

Semen handling｜Inspection and preservation｜Measure semen in prescribed amounts and load insemination guns, assess density and motility under a microscope, dilute by formula, package and label, and record origin and quality.

Animal health｜Observation and immunization｜Observe estrus and disease or injury symptoms, treat minor illnesses and injuries and contact veterinarians for serious illness, and immunize via drinking-water medication, injection, or powder spraying.

Identification and records｜Pedigree and production data｜Mark individuals with ear notches or ear tags, and record weight, growth curves, rations, and estrus, parturition, mating, and semen-use records.

Supply, sales, and showing｜Purchasing and sales｜Purchase and stock feed and medications, arrange sales of animals and eggs to hospitals, research centers, pet stores, and food processing enterprises, and take animals to shows.

hero.quick_answer: Animal Breeders select and breed animals according to their lineage, traits, and offspring, possibly needing to master artificial insemination techniques and equipment use, and record estrus, parturition intervals, and pedigrees: feed and water animals and clean and disinfect housing, observe estrus and judge mating timing, select breeding animals and semen samples and perform artificial insemination, examine and dilute semen, observe disease and injury and immunize, mark individuals and record production data, and purchase feed and medications and arrange sales and showing. This page presents US OEWS Animal Breeders-specific wage percentiles and BLS employment projections; the China side provides only industry-scope and Animal Husbandry Law framework references; this page is not veterinary advice.
